title: Seizure
summary: Protect from injury, time the seizure, and call for prolonged, first, repeated, or complicated seizures.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Seizures
actions: Clear hard or dangerous objects away and cushion the head with something soft.
Time the seizure from its start. Do not restrain the movements.
After convulsions stop, check breathing. Use the recovery position if breathing normally and stay calmly with the person.

Call emergency services for a first seizure, duration over 5 minutes, repeated seizures without recovery, seizure in water, significant injury, breathing difficulty, pregnancy, an infant younger than 6 months, or no return to usual alertness within 5 to 10 minutes.
Start CPR if normal breathing does not resume.
prohibitions: Do not put anything in the mouth.
Do not hold the person down or try to stop the movements.
Do not give food, drink, or oral medicine until fully alert and able to swallow.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for a seizure longer than 5 minutes, a first seizure, repeated seizures without recovery, injury, water involvement, breathing trouble, pregnancy, or failure to return to baseline.
